frame: Rater frame: precision first. Omit a guarantee unless the packet names a deployed artifact and a locator. Score the protocol as an element of the agentic commerce stack, not as a standalone product. Kleros is scored as a candidate L8 for agent-speed commerce, not as a general-purpose court.

C.promise: Scoped signed payment mandates resolve L4 moral hazard / commitment
C.evidence: Intent Mandate and Cart Mandate as tamper-proof VCs; chain of evidence intent→cart→payment method
C.failure: Revocation not consistently propagated into settlement (T4)

I.promise: Binding to UCP for payment-mandate linkage
I.evidence: UCP spec references AP2 mandates and VCs; AP2 blog lists A2A×x402 extension with Coinbase/EF/MetaMask
I.failure: One-sided ecosystem binding; no cross-layer auditable proof

A.promise: Cryptographically signed mandates scope authorization; partial audit trail
A.evidence: Signed Intent/Cart Mandates as W3C VCs; non-repudiable audit trail for authorization
A.failure: No agent-speed dispute forum; no delivery-proof bind
A.metric: Proportion of mandated actions within consent scope; revocation propagation rate

EM.promise: Reduces reliance on one or two institutions (cards, KYC bureau)
EM.evidence: Payment-agnostic: cards, stablecoins, RTGS supported; stablecoin option reduces banking dependence
EM.failure: Still requires card/RTP rails as primary fallback
EM.metric: Fraction of flows operable without bank account

S.promise: Public versioned spec with named governance
S.evidence: Public GitHub repo (github.com/google-agentic-commerce/AP2); 60+ named industry collaborators
S.failure: No standards-body process yet; reference impls incomplete
S.metric: Number of independent implementations; versioned spec releases

C.promise: Cryptographic payment proof (HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-SIGNATURE) addresses L5 moral hazard / payment
C.evidence: HTTP 402 flow with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; facilitator verifies and settles; exact/upto/batch-settlement schemes
C.failure: Payment completion distinct from service delivery (T3)
C.metric: Time from proof-of-payment to service invocation

I.promise: Optional bindings to AP2 and ERC-8004
I.evidence: AP2 blog: A2A×x402 extension; ERC-8004 abstract: proofOfPayment in off-chain feedback file
I.failure: Both bindings are optional/suggested, not required
I.metric: Count of protocols with auditable x402 bindings

A.evidence: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE for auth; signed receipts (optional) for audit
A.failure: No native subjective-quality forum; irreversibility is recourse deficit
A.metric: Ratio of on-chain proof to total settlement volume

EM.promise: Operable without banks, cards, KYC, or platform identity
EM.evidence: No account signup or KYC in base flow; blockchain-agnostic (EVM/Solana/Algorand); CAIP-2 network IDs
EM.failure: Needs stablecoin availability and blockchain infrastructure
EM.metric: Fraction of flows without banking/KYC dependency

S.promise: Versioned spec with multiple independent implementations under Linux Foundation governance
S.evidence: Linux Foundation x402 Foundation; 75.41M tx / $24.24M vol (30d); TS/Go/Python SDKs; middleware for Express/Next/Hono/FastAPI
S.failure: IETF receipts still drafts; refund/compliance not finalized
S.metric: Number of independent SDKs; Foundation governance status

C.promise: Post-purchase lifecycle state (fulfillment/refund) addresses L6 incomplete contracts
C.evidence: Order object with fulfillment events (delivered), tracking, adjustments/refund; capability negotiation with version dates
C.failure: Post-purchase state and refund portability remain merchant-specific (T4)
C.metric: Portability of order/refund objects across merchant implementations

I.promise: First-class transport and mandate bindings to MCP, A2A, AP2
I.evidence: UCP spec: 'Built-in support for AP2, A2A, MCP'; A2A transport via Agent Card URL; MCP as first-class transport
I.failure: Bindings are inclusion claims without cross-protocol verification
I.metric: Number of cross-protocol binding clauses with verification

A.promise: OAuth 2.0 identity linking with AP2 mandate authorization
A.evidence: Identity linking (OAuth 2.0); AP2 mandates and VCs for payment authorization; refund adjustments
A.failure: No native agent-speed dispute protocol; economic finality via PSP, not UCP
A.metric: Proportion of flows with AP2-mandated authorization

EM.promise: Hybrid rail (MoR+AP2) operable where courts/banks are weak
EM.evidence: Web2-origin protocol with stablecoin + card fallback; `continue_url` degrades to web storefront
EM.failure: PSP/card dependency remains for economic finality
EM.metric: Fraction of flows operable without PSP intervention

S.promise: Co-developed spec with major retail/payment firms
S.evidence: Endorsed by Google, Shopify, Walmart, Stripe, Visa; public GitHub repo; versioned spec at ucp.dev/latest/specification/
S.failure: Lodging/food specs incomplete; thin corpus n=36
S.metric: Number of endorsing firms; spec completeness per vertical

C.promise: Portable identity plus behavioral trust addresses L1 adverse selection / identity
C.evidence: Three on-chain registries: Identity (ERC-721 + URIStorage), Reputation (giveFeedback/revoke/appendResponse), Validation (request/response hooks)
C.failure: Sybil inflation; fragmented reputation; capability claims not cryptographically guaranteed (T1)
C.metric: Sybil-resistance score per namespace; cross-registry consistency rate

I.promise: Discovery bindings to A2A/MCP/ENS/DID; optional x402 support
I.evidence: Registration file lists A2A/MCP/ENS/DID/wallet endpoints; optional `x402Support`; `proofOfPayment` in feedback
I.failure: Pointers, not auditable bindings; cross-chain reputation unaggregated
I.metric: Count of protocols with verified ERC-8004 binding

A.evidence: `getSummary` requires clientAddresses filter to mitigate Sybil; validation hooks for stakers/zkML/TEE
A.failure: Reputation scores don't bind AP2 mandate terms or x402 conditions
A.metric: Correlation between reputation score and mandate-compliance rate

EM.evidence: Deployable as per-chain singleton on L2 or mainnet; no KYC dependency
EM.failure: Needs blockchain infrastructure and wallet access
EM.metric: Fraction of flows operable without traditional finance

S.evidence: EIP-8004 draft; authors include MetaMask, EF, Google, Coinbase; Magicians thread
S.failure: Draft status; no canonical mainnet singleton address
S.metric: EIP finalization status; number of deployable instances

C.promise: Machine-readable capability discovery addresses L2 adverse selection
C.evidence: Open standard connecting AI apps to tools/data/workflows; prompts/resources/tools/completions; versioned docs 2026-07-28
C.failure: Advertised capability not bound to demonstrated competence (T2)

I.promise: Transport layer for UCP and A2A
I.evidence: UCP treats MCP as first-class transport; A2A docs distinguish MCP (agent-to-tool) from A2A (agent-to-agent)
I.failure: No payment, settlement, or L8 artifact specified
I.metric: Count of protocols with formal MCP binding

A.evidence: User-mediated trust model; explicit delegation boundary
A.failure: Tool-call logs don't prove intent fidelity; governance gaps
A.metric: Proportion of tool calls within delegated scope

EM.evidence: Clients: Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor; broad SDK ecosystem

S.promise: Versioned open standard with broad independent implementations
S.evidence: versioned docs 2026-07-28; broad client list; measurement study of ecosystem
S.failure: No security section extracted; governance gaps noted

C.promise: Agent-to-agent task routing and lifecycle traces address L3 moral hazard / effort
C.evidence: Agent Card with identity/capabilities/endpoint; Task with unique ID and lifecycle; request/response polling, SSE, webhooks
C.failure: Task completion doesn't prove intent fidelity (T2)
C.metric: Rate of task-completion vs. intent-fidelity discrepancy

I.promise: Explicitly complementary to MCP; AP2 extension for payments
I.evidence: A2A docs: 'MCP = agent-to-tool; A2A = agent-to-agent'; AP2 described as A2A extension
I.failure: No payment or dispute mechanism in A2A itself

A.promise: Auth declared on Agent Card; credentials in HTTP headers
A.evidence: Agent Card declares auth requirements; opaque agents (no shared memory/tools)
A.failure: Overprivilege, long-lived tokens, missing consent in payment/identity (arxiv)

EM.promise: Reduces platform dependence via direct agent-to-agent communication
EM.failure: Still requires OAuth credentials and infrastructure
EM.metric: Dependency reduction index vs. web2 platforms

S.promise: Versioned spec with official SDKs and LF governance
S.evidence: Linux Foundation project; SDKs: Python, JS, Java, C#, Go, Rust; TSC with major vendors
S.failure: No tagged spec record in corpus; relies on live fetch
S.metric: Number of official SDKs; LF governance status

C.promise: Event-based agent↔user interaction layer addresses L7 information revelation
C.evidence: Streaming chat, multimodality, generative UI, shared state, HITL interrupts (pause/approve/edit/retry)
C.failure: Interface transparency doesn't create enforceable remedy (T5)
C.metric: Rate of UI-intent vs. executed-action discrepancy

I.evidence: Docs: 'agent↔user layer next to MCP (tools) and A2A (agents)'; framework integrations
I.failure: No specified binding to payment or dispute protocols

A.evidence: Interrupts and observability documented; no mandate, settlement, or dispute objects
A.failure: Protocol does not make agents auditable for L4/L5/L8 properties

EM.promise: Reduces platform trust dependence via explicit UI control
EM.evidence: Many framework integrations (LangGraph, CrewAI, ADK, etc.); terminal and chat clients

S.evidence: Open protocol; SDKs in Kotlin/Go/Dart/Java/Rust; CopilotKit partnership origin
S.failure: No spec record in corpus (n=1 false positive); no governance body identified
S.metric: Number of framework integrations; governance documentation

C.promise: Smart-contract arbitrator provides L8 contract enforcement
C.evidence: Crowdsourced jurors stake PNK, vote, earn rewards; escrow product with dispute resolution; appeals and court hierarchy; ERC-792/ERC-1497 standards
C.failure: Latency is days, not agent-speed (T6, T8)
C.metric: Mean resolution time vs. agent transaction speed

I.promise: Not wired into AP2/x402/UCP as default L8
I.evidence: No specified binding to any lower-layer protocol
I.failure: Evidence ≠ remedy unless forum and consequence are wired (T6)
I.metric: Count of lower-layer protocols with Kleros L8 binding

A.evidence: Escrow product holds funds with built-in dispute resolution; evidence submission via ERC-1497
A.failure: Subjective quality judged but not at machine transaction speed; enterprise focus is days-scale
A.metric: Proportion of disputes resolved within agent-speed SLA

EM.evidence: Smart-contract based; Schelling-point incentives; cross-jurisdictional potential
EM.failure: Cross-jurisdiction enforcement not automatic; days-scale latency

S.evidence: Court, Curate, Proof of Humanity, Escrow, Scout, Governor, Reality.eth products; Snapshot voting
S.failure: Not a native agentic-commerce standard; thin corpus (n=3 OA)
